Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the company or Huang potentially knew about chips being diverted to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen."

"Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that that the president is saying to the American people ... It shouldn't be what my message would be either," Blanche said.
While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the announcement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.
The company's share price was down more than 7% in early afternoon trading, but remained well above the level it closed at on Friday, before Huang's return was announced.

The company's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn on its original position. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, said Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".
The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.
On Monday, Trump said he spoke to the company's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang.
There has been bipartisan political anger over Huang's reinstatement.

Republican representative Don Bacon said Nvidia should have "ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang", while Republican senator Pete Ricketts said Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".

Democratic representative Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, said Trump's "direct involvement" with Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions", and Democratic senator Ruben Gallego said Congress needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".

articles.headline: This hidden iOS 27 feature ensures you’ll never sleep through an alarm again
keyFacts: A new iOS 27 feature allows users to set alarm and timer volumes independently from ringtone and alert volumes.
The independent volume control prevents users from accidentally missing alarms when their ringtone volume is turned down.
Users can adjust this setting by turning off Match Ringtone Volume under Sounds and Haptics in iPhone Settings.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- An iOS 27 setting that lets you set your alarm volume independently of your ringtone volume.
- The feature addresses the problem of your alarm volume being subject to your ringtone settings.
- With it, you can turn your alarm volume all the way up when your ringtone is quieter.

A lesser-known iOS 27 feature includes a new alarm volume setting that gives alarms, timers, and ringtones independent volume control. You can adjust the volume settings for alarms and timers independently of your phone’s alerts and system sounds, so you don’t miss an alarm after lowering your ringtone volume.
There have been ways to adjust the iPhone alarm volume for a few years, but there’s an important distinction between what the new feature entails and what those methods involve.
More from ZDNET

Previously, you could adjust your Sleep Schedule alarms to always go off at a specific volume, regardless of the iPhone’s shared volume. Sleep Schedule alarms have a dedicated volume slider that you can set and adjust as needed, all configured within the Sleep focus. The new feature, however, lets you set an independent volume for all alarms and timers, not just those in the Sleep Schedule.
How to independently adjust your alarm volume
- Go to your iPhone Settings.
- Find Sounds & Haptics.
- Scroll down to find the toggle for Alarms and Timers.
- Turn off Match Ringtone Volume.
- Set your preferred alarm volume.
Alarms, Timers, Alerts, and System Sounds are set to match your ringtone volume by default, but you can turn them off in the Sounds and Haptics setting.

Once you disable the option to match your alarm volume to your ringtone’s volume, you can set your volume for upcoming alarms. With this feature, you can maximize your alarm volume without affecting the volume of incoming calls and notifications.

articles.headline: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe
keyFacts: An Amazon delivery drone crashed onto a Michigan garage roof after striking a fiber-optic cable on November 20.
The Amazon MK30 drone model features sense-and-avoid technology meant to prevent collisions with obstacles.
The Federal Aviation Administration is investigating the crash, while the National Transportation Safety Board is considering a probe.
body: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. It’s the latest delivery drone mishap caught on video as Amazon and other companies are ramping up such aerial delivery operations across the United States.

The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and being surprised by a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit. After the drone dropped the package into Brennan’s backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor’s garage roof and some power lines.
“Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan told WXYZ 7.

Amazon Prime Air currently operates a fleet of battery-powered MK30 drones that can deliver packages weighing up to five pounds and have onboard sense-and-avoid technology to avoid obstacles. However, the drone clearly failed to avoid the thin fiber-optic cable in this case—so hopefully the FAA investigation would take that into account along with Amazon delivery drone procedures.

The FAA preliminary accident and incident notification briefly describes the incident as “UAS struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff.” That notice was posted on November 23.

The National Transportation Safety Board is also gathering information about the incident but has not yet decided whether to open its own probe, according to CNBC. That US government agency holds primary responsibility for investigating aviation accidents and other transportation incidents.

articles.headline: Studio founded by former Apex Legends leaders is closing without releasing a game
keyFacts: Gravity Well, a studio founded by former Apex Legends leaders, is entering hibernation after losing funding for its game.
The studio shuttered without releasing a game, following the layoff of over 40 employees last month.
Gravity Well leadership stated they are open to hearing from investors or publishers interested in supporting their project.
body: Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time.

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good."

But like so many other ambitious new studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain."
A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation."

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation."
The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

articles.headline: The Steam Awards turn 10 with throwback categories and a Game of the Year Hall of Fame
keyFacts: Valve opened nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards, which include returning categories and a new Game of the Year Hall of Fame.
Users can nominate games across 14 categories until November 30 at 6pm UK time.
Finalists will be revealed on December 17, with winners announced after voting closes on January 2.
body: Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards are now open, and to mark the event's 10th anniversary, Valve has brought back some categories from years past and added a Hall of Fame.

You've got until 6pm UK (10am Pacific) on 30th November to nominate your favourite games of the year across 14 categories. Returning throwbacks include Just 5 More Minutes, Defies Description, and This is My Job Now, which recognises games that simulate mundane real-life jobs.
The new Hall of Fame category will appear when voting opens, and will let players choose their favourite from Steam's previous Game of the Year winners to crown the best game of the past decade.
Most categories are only open to games released on Steam since last year's Autumn Sale.

The exception is the Labo(u)r of Love award, which goes to older games that developers are still supporting with new content. Previous Labo(u)r of Love winners, including Warframe, Grand Theft Auto 5, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3, can't be nominated again.

Five finalists will be revealed in each category when voting opens alongside the Steam Winter Sale on 17th December. Voting closes at 10am Pacific on 2nd January, and the winners will be announced straight afterwards.
Nominating in at least one category also earns you the first level of Steam's Nomination Committee badge.
Earlier this month, Valve released a new Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

articles.headline: WoW: Forever’s Best Buffs Now Work As Intended
keyFacts: Blizzard released a hotfix for World of Warcraft: Forever that allows World Buffs to persist across loading screens.
Players can now retain these stat-boosting effects when entering dungeons to improve their health and damage output.
Blizzard stated that World Buffs will still be removed when players enter raid instances.
body: World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.

World Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events. The most common World Buff players see is Warchief's Blessing on the Horde and the new Might of Stormwind for the Alliance, which are granted to all players in Orgrimmar, Stormwind, and their surrounding low-level zones when players on their respective faction turn in a specific high-level quest.

Now that players are reaching endgame and turning in the required quest, these buffs are popping off constantly. They grant a whopping 300 hit points, 15% melee haste, and 10 mana regen per five seconds for one hour. At lower levels, those are some serious stats, particularly the 300 HP.

Unfortunately, players haven't been able to take full advantage of the buffs, as a bug was causing them to be lost when hitting a loading screen. That meant any time a group stepped into a dungeon or took a boat or zeppelin to a new location, their World Buffs would be removed.

That has finally been fixed in the latest update, so players can now enter dungeons with World Buffs to help maximize their damage and health. This should be particularly useful for doing dungeons at a slightly lower level than is intended, as the extra HP and melee haste is definitely noticable.

Blizzard clarified in the patch notes that World Buffs will still be removed when entering raids, so players won't be able to stack as many World Buffs as possible before raid night, as was the case in previous versions of classic WoW.

Other changes found in the patch notes include a fix for an Uldaman boss that players were exploiting to make fast gold. Another is a fix for "a few spells and abilities" that were causing more weapon-proc effects than intended, likely nerfing the DPS of whatever classes were taking advantage of the bug. You can read the full patch notes below.

Blizzard recently outlined in the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast how it wants to get rid of the idea of "best-in-slot gear," as well as how the game's has overhauled old-school WoW's player-vs.-player systems . In other Forever news, the game's launch has seen more than 15 million characters created so far, with the highest weekly player numbers for WoW in 15 years .

articles.headline: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
keyFacts: Anthropic stock fell below its $83 IPO price to as low as $76 a share on Tuesday.
Observers say Anthropic's stock performance serves as a barometer for how public market investors value the AI sector.
Continued poor trading could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies.
body: Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83, trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close.
Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value.

The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector.

The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share. If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies.

Anthropic isn’t the only AI stock selling off on Tuesday. Nvidia fell more than 7% by midday, giving back some of the more than 30%-plus gain it posted Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.

President Trump said he spoke directly with Nvidia's board to push for Huang's return.

“He’s got a very, very, very good wife, and they’ve worked it out,” Trump told The New York Times. “She’s a fantastic woman.”

articles.headline: Paul Scholes says ‘rabbit in the headlights’ £52m Man United man is not Premier League level
keyFacts: Paul Scholes criticized Manchester United defender Leny Yoro, claiming he does not look like a Premier League level player.
Yoro received a straight red card during a 4-0 loss to Liverpool, though the Football Association later overturned the suspension after a successful appeal.
Former teammate Nicky Butt suggested Yoro would have been sent out on loan for development during his era at the club.
body: Paul Scholes has claimed the Premier League looks too much for Leny Yoro after Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.
Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United’s embarrassing loss at Anfield as the Mauricio Pochettino era got off to a nightmare start.
Yoro has come in for added scrutiny after his sending off against Liverpool AFP
The Frenchman clumsily ran into the back of Alexander Isak as the Reds striker ran in on goal and cut across his path.
Yoro was controversially shown a straight red card, as Liverpool went on to run riot against the ten-man Red Devils after Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the subsequent free-kick.
While the defender was set to serve a one-match suspension for his dismissal, this has since been overturned after an appeal .
The FA confirmed on Tuesday that the ban had been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.
However, the circumstances surrounding Yoro’s red gave him little defence in the eyes of Man United great Paul Scholes , who has criticised him in the aftermath of the Liverpool defeat.
Scholes raises questions
Since arriving at Old Trafford as a highly-rated 18-year-old in a deal worth £60million in 2024, Yoro has endured a rollercoaster ride in his 78 United appearances so far.
His most difficult period yet has come this term, forming part of leaky Red Devils defence that has conceded 23 goals in 11 Premier League matches – with only Crystal Palace conceding more .
And while none of United’s defenders earned praise for Sunday’s display, club icon Scholes took aim at Yoro on Monday .
Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football , he said: “The Premier League at this minute just looks a little bit too much for him.
“You know what, he’s come in to a really bad set-up defensively now. I think they also made the point yesterday if he went in next to [Virgil] Van Dijk he might look a little bit better.
Yoro tripped up Alexander Isak and was sent off against Liverpool, which immediately left his side facing an uphill battle Getty
“But he doesn’t look Premier League level. He looks like a rabbit in the headlights.”

Scholes was joined by former United teammate Nicky Butt , who agreed that Yoro’s level of performance would have seen him sent out on loan during their days together under Sir Alex Ferguson between 1994 and 2004.
Butt added: “If that’s Man United in our day, he’s on loan like a Jonny Evans or a John O’Shea.
“He’s a great talent that will come good.”
However, Scholes was sceptical of Yoro’s label as a future star, which has seen him eyed up by European champions Paris Saint-Germain .
The Premier League great replied: “I’m not sure how much of a great talent he is.
Yoro is yet to convince everyone in his two years at Old Trafford Getty
“I think he has shown a little bit of a sign in the France squad but every time I’ve seen him he doesn’t look at the races.
“Everything’s happening around him and he’s just a bit, ‘Oh, what do I do?'”
Yoro has struggled to make one of the centre-back starting roles his own since signing for the Red Devils in the summer of 2024.
He had to wait until October 10 for his first Premier League start of this season, playing just under an hour in the 1-1 draw with Tottenham.
Since then, he has been a mainstay in United’s back line amid a poor run of form which leaves them a lowly 19th in the Premier League.
Yoro has also started three of his side’s four Champions League games this term, missing the 4-1 thrashing by Como after he was shown a red card in a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid .

articles.headline: 'I miss being on court' - Sinner has 'minor surgery' on knee
keyFacts: World number two Jannik Sinner underwent minor surgery to treat an injury to his iliotibial band.
Sinner has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon in July and missed the end of the 2025 season.
Sinner will now begin a recovery process with his team ahead of the Australian Open in January.
body: - Published
World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins.
The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July.
In a post on Instagram, Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee.
"Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," the 25-year-old wrote.
"After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we'd all hoped.
"I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team."
Earlier in November, Sinner said his goal was to go to Australia and potentially "play a few tournaments" before the first Grand Slam of the year begins on 17 January.
However, the Italian has also stressed the need to think of his long-term career in protecting his body.
The Instagram post is the first time Sinner has specified what the knee issue is.
In a video posted on his Youtube channel in October, Sinner said he had also lost "a lot of weight" after having his tonsils removed.
He also described having "days where I felt nothing and could play without any problems, and then days where I couldn't move at all".
He suffered a nasty fall in the first match of his Wimbledon title defence and also had blood seeping through his shoes because of a problematic toenail.
Alexander Zverev has become world number one in Sinner's absence, while rival Carlos Alcaraz swept four titles after returning from his injury lay-off in September.
Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches.
He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters', and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way.
However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title.
Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece.
He ended his season in early October, meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025.
Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking.
Having met in three of the four Grand Slam finals last year, Sinner and Alcaraz played each other only once in 2026.
Sinner won their final at the Monte Carlo Masters shortly before Alcaraz spent four months out with a wrist injury.
Alcaraz's victory at the season-ending ATP Finals means he is only 350 ranking points behind Sinner - although the Spaniard will be defending 2,000 of those at the Australian Open.
"It's a shame we don't have Jannik," Alcaraz told SuperTennis TV, external after winning the ATP Finals on Sunday.
"We really miss him. I have not seen him for many months right now since I got injured in April.
"I can't wait to see him fit, healthy. I am pretty sure that he is going to come back even better and stronger."
Alcaraz will be the defending champion in Melbourne, having beaten Djokovic to complete a historic career Grand Slam in January.

articles.headline: Arm strongarms site that hosts ad-free documentation and it may disappear
keyFacts: Arm lawyers demanded developer Jon Palmisciano take down his website hosting simplified Arm documentation by December 4 over alleged copyright and trademark violations.
Palmisciano created the ad-free site to help developers browse Arm documentation, while Arm stated it must protect its brand and copyrighted technical content.
Palmisciano expects the site to close soon and may open-source his site-building tools, while Arm said it hopes to open a constructive dialogue.
body: Arm is swinging the hammer at an enthusiast’s site hosting a bloat-free version of its instruction reference documentation, demanding it be taken offline after several years of availability.

The demand from Arm lawyers to Jon Palmisciano concern Jon’s Arm Reference , a site that provides the same arm Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) info available on Arm’s site, but with what Palmisciano describes as “without a million popups and all of the bloat” that Arm provides on its own.

According to Palmisciano, his copy of the Arm ISA was culled from machine-readable XML files and stripped of the bloat. He built his version in 2022 with new CSS on top of it, and the addition of a quick search feature that, according to his comments on Hacker News, isn’t available in the official version.

“The aim has always been to make it the most comfortable and bullshit-free browsing experience for people who need these docs daily,” Palmisciano wrote in HN. Based on the responses the site seems to have plenty of fans.

That doesn’t matter to Arm, though: As far as the lawyers are concerned, Palmisciano’s site is a copyright violation due to its use of Arm trademarks and inclusion of copyrighted reference material for the Armv9-A and Armv9-A architecture.

Arm doesn’t care if Palmisciano’s project is well intentioned or for the benefit of the many software developers that write code for its chipsets, either: They want it offline by December 4 – 10 days from the publication of this story – or else.
As for what is going to happen, it seems like Jon’s Arm Reference will likely cease to exist in a little over a week – at least in its current form.

“Ideally I'd love to just get permission from Arm to keep the site up, but I'm pretty pessimistic about that,” Promisciano told us. That said, Promisciano has “already seen a few archives and mirrors already.” The HN thread discussing the takedown order includes links to several versions, and Promisciano has another trick up his sleeve that he’s considering playing: Open-sourcing the software he used to build his ISA page.

“I'd also consider open-sourcing my tooling so that people can (for their own private use) turn the original XML downloads from Arm into an identical site they can host locally,” Promisciano told us. He said that he'll likely tweet about opening the tooling if he does do so. He's also considered directing the URL for Jon's Arm reference to point to the open-source tool, but Arm wants the subdomain it's hosted on removed from his site as well, so that may not happen.
Arm has been in touch to defend itself as well, saying that Arm appreciates the efforts of people like Promisciano, but that it still has to protect its brand, and documentation.

"We have a responsibility to ensure Arm is the primary source of technical resources and information and to protect the Arm brand," an Arm spokesperson told us. "Striking the right balance between third parties sharing helpful peer-to-peer resources while ensuring copyrighted Arm-related technical content is accurate has been critical to building the thriving ecosystem we have today."

In other words, if you’re an Arm dev worried about losing a valuable resource and having to turn to a website that bombards you with junk just to look up a few simple opcodes and operands you’d better find a backup host before next month.
That said, Arm is willing to work something out with Promisciano, the company told us.

"We have recently flagged our concerns with regard to the use of Arm copyright content and the Arm brand on this website and shared the Arm trademark guidelines," Arm explained. "Our hope is to open a constructive dialogue, and we've asked that the website owner reach out as we seek to resolve this."
As Promisciano posted on HN, Arm is asking for removal of its trademark and copyrighted documentation. That, Promisciano said, "seems hard to work around while still keeping the site useful." ®

articles.headline: Chris Van Hollen wants to replace Chuck Schumer. We asked him why.
keyFacts: Senator Chris Van Hollen is challenging Senator Chuck Schumer for leadership of the Senate Democratic caucus.
Van Hollen said the caucus needs a fresh face to better confront Donald Trump and take on special interests.
Senate Democrats will hold a vote on December 1 to decide their leadership for the new Congress.
body: “We've been given this big opportunity, with 56 senators. We cannot blow it, and we need to show people that we're going to deliver and fight for them,” Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), who is challenging Sen. Chuck Schumer for majority leader, said on America, Actually. | Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images
Change is coming to Washington, DC, next Congress — and one Democratic senator thinks that that should also mean a change in leadership for the new Senate majority.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) is challenging Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY), who has led the party’s caucus in the upper chamber for a decade, for the top job in the new Congress. Van Hollen, who previously served in the House before being elected to the Senate in 2016, said the party needs a fresh face to deliver the change voters demanded when they handed Dems such big victories in the midterms.

In an interview on Vox’s America, Actually podcast, Van Hollen told host Astead Herndon that Schumer has been too timid in confronting Trump and the Republican Party, and too unwilling to use unconventional means to try to rally support for Democratic causes.

“My view is that working outside the Congress to highlight the attacks on our democracy was essential. You can’t just use the same tools that were used before Trump to take on a lawless Trump,” Van Hollen said. “We need to organize in this moment to help protect our democracy and our Constitution and get things done and deliver.”
Herndon spoke with Van Hollen ahead of the December 1 vote that will decide the chamber’s Democratic leadership for the new Congress; below is an excerpt of their, edited for length and clarity.

There’s much more in the full show, including how Van Hollen would handle the looming government funding deadline and a possible shutdown over the Iran war; his approach to reining in funding for Israel and finding a path forward to improve the US healthcare system; and his plans for holding the Trump administration accountable.
You can listen to America, Actually wherever you get your podcasts or watch it on Vox’s YouTube channel .
You’re running for Senate majority leader, challenging Chuck Schumer. What pushed you to raise your hand?

When I saw the results of this election, which was a sweeping crying out from the American people about the need for change, my view was that this was clearly a rejection of the policies of Donald Trump. But Democrats were still on probation, and I don’t think we earned people’s trust by simply going back to the status quo.
We’ve been given this big opportunity, with 56 senators . We cannot blow it, and we need to show people that we’re going to deliver and fight for them.

You’ve also been in office a long time. You’ve been close to the Democratic establishment. How do the politics of Chris Von Hollen represent what the Democratic base was crying out for more than the politics of Chuck Schumer?
If you look at my public service, there are many times that I have taken on the Democratic establishment, but you’re right. I was part of Speaker Pelosi’s leadership team in the House.

This election, in my view, was a message of economic populism : People saying they want to take on a system that’s rigged in favor of the very wealthy, against working people, and fueled by political corruption. My record has been taking on big money special interests for the public good.

If you look at all the issues our candidates ran on, there’s going to be an army of lobbyists descending on Washington, DC, in the Capitol to eat away at what Democrats said they wanted to do. My view is you need someone with a record of taking on those interests at this very important moment.
“This should not be a one-man band. We need more of our team having meaningful roles to deliver for the American people.”
Are the issues with Schumer one of tactics or one of communication? Where have his failings been?

If you look at the issues that we want to advance right now, which is taking on a tax code that’s rigged in favor of people who make money off of money and against people who earn a paycheck through hard work, or the ambitious changes that we need to make in our very broken healthcare system — which has become a money-making system, not a healthcare system — then it’s important that you have somebody leading the Democratic caucus who has been fighting for those issues every single day.

I will also say I don’t think we want a Democratic leader who intervenes in open, contested Democratic primaries. I’ve got two colleagues, senators-elect from Michigan and from Minnesota, who would not be there if Senator Schumer had had his way because he sided with AIPAC and crypto and other special interests like Big Pharma, in the case of Michigan, against a candidate who was more the people’s candidate.
I don’t think we should be interfering in those primaries, and I also think we need more democracy in the United States Senate, and I think my colleagues agree.
Can you give me an example of a negotiation that Schumer has handled in Trump’s second term that you would do differently?

I do believe that early on in this administration many of us recognized the threat that this administration posed to our democracy and to our Constitution. That was around the time that the Trump administration abducted a constituent of mine, Kilmar Abrego Garcia , and took him down to a gulag in El Salvador. I went down there to see if he was dead or alive and ultimately bring him back, in order to protect his due process rights.

My view is that there should have been much more intense resistance from the Senate early on in those days. That would have meant early on confronting the president, and refusing to provide additional money and funding for some of his lawless activities.
What does that look like?

That would be essentially saying, “Mr. President, we’re not going to give you this blank check in order to carry out these attacks on our Constitution, to see these ICE raids where they were undermining constitutional rights, killing American citizens in the streets of Minneapolis.”

All of that needed to be resisted early on. I helped organize the first protest demonstration against Elon Musk taking his chainsaw to USAID . We also went to highlight that lawlessness in front of other federal agencies. My view is that working outside the Congress to highlight the attacks on our democracy was essential. You can’t just use the same tools that were used before Trump to take on a lawless Trump.
It sounds like you’re talking about making the position more of an activist organizer position and leading from the front more than we saw Schumer do over the last couple years.
That is fair. I do think that, especially with our new members. They need to be front and center. But we need to put everyone’s talents forward.
The bottom line is, we need to organize in this moment to help protect our democracy and our Constitution and get things done and deliver.
The magic number for any Senate leader is 28 . Chuck Schumer has said he has 16 declared supporters. I think that includes himself. You have five. What is the whip count?

We’re now north of 15. We have momentum in our favor. Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan supported me, which shows that this is not a progressive versus moderate thing. It really is a question of taking on an economy rigged for the wealthy against working people. That is the framework in which our candidates pursued this election.

I think that that is what unifies us all going forward. But to do that, it is important to have someone with a history and a record of taking on big money special interests to advance the public interest.
North of 15 is still 13 short of 28 , though, if my math is correct.

You’re right. There are a lot of people who are very undecided. The longer this debate goes on, the discussion goes on, the more people want to change how we organize ourselves in the caucus. This should not be a one-man band. We need more of our team having meaningful roles to deliver for the American people.

articles.headline: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
keyFacts: Jared Kushner's partners bought 300 acres of Albanian oceanfront land for over $130 million to build a resort.
Albanian prosecutors and locals claim the land was illegally acquired through forged property titles.
An investigation by Albanian prosecutors into the forged titles could halt the resort project.
body: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?

ZVERNEC, Albania — In the summer of 2021, Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump boarded a yacht owned by Nat Rothschild, an heir to the European banking family. On the way from Montenegro to Greece, the yacht anchored off the coast of Albania.
And, as Kushner told an investment conference last year, that's when Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama arrived at the boat to tell them about his plan for the country.

"I was very impressed by what he wanted to do with the country," said Kushner. "I really didn't know anything about the country and I didn't understand the history, and the darkness of the history with the communism and terrible leadership led to it being fully undeveloped as a nation."

A year later, Kushner was looking for development opportunities in the Balkans. He returned to the Albanian coast — to the city of Vlore, which was finishing the construction of an airport atop a wetland near an undeveloped coastline. "And obviously, a country's going to build an airport by the coast in a place they think is most beautiful," Kushner told the conference, "so we went there and we were looking for opportunities, and we found some incredible opportunities."

Kushner found those opportunities at Hidrovor Beach, an expanse of caramel-colored sand along the southern Albanian coast, with the gentle waves of the Adriatic lapping its perimeter and a view of an uninhabited island. A company working for Kushner purchased this land and 300 acres surrounding it for more than $130 million in April. But several people here tell NPR this is not Kushner's land.
They say it's theirs.
Land grabs and falsified documents

"This land here belonged to my family for centuries," says Gentian Mocka, who claims his family has owned this strip of beach and wetland since the time of the Ottoman Empire. He provided NPR land titles that appear to prove this.
After World War II, Albania's Communist government seized it — along with all private land.

When communism fell in 1991, families like Mocka's embarked on a years-long process to get their land back. "But then our problems started with the guys that were much more powerful than we were — had a lot of political support, were very rich and very well connected with the politics of that time," says Mocka.

In 2005, Mocka learned that someone else was laying claim to his family's land — a fellow Albanian named Artur Shehu. It was a familiar name for those who lived here in the 1990s, when the regional capital of Vlore was outside the control of the country's government. It was instead run by mafia-style gangs. At the time, Shehu was well-known to police in Vlore for his alleged involvement in a crime syndicate that, according to Albanian prosecutors, smuggled drugs and migrants into Europe. He fled Albania in 1999, after what police say was a shootout with a rival gang.

He ended up in the United States, where he received asylum in 2001 and, later, became a U.S. citizen. The 60-year-old Shehu now lives in a villa in Miami Beach. But he's continued to manage a growing real estate portfolio back in Albania through an associate in Vlore named Pellumb Petritaj.

The pair has claimed plots of land — including Mocka's family plot — up and down the southern Albanian coast, and prosecutors have taken notice. In 2018, Petritaj served three years in prison for forging land titles on behalf of Shehu. And on Nov. 18, Petritaj was sentenced to another seven years in prison for falsifying documents to $17 million worth of oceanfront property in the city of Vlore on behalf of Shehu. The court ordered the land — which does not include Mocka's family plot — confiscated from Shehu last week. The pair has also claimed oceanfront farmland in the village of Zvernec, adjacent to Mocka's land.
Albanian prosecutors say land linked to Kushner may have been "illegally acquired"
The pair has also claimed oceanfront farmland in the village of Zvernec, adjacent to Mocka's land.

The quiet village has only a couple hundred residents. Most of them, like Minella Konomi and Natasha Kota, are past the age of 70. On a recent warm and sunny afternoon, the two are resting on benches in the courtyard of the village church after a day of harvesting olives. They nod their heads when asked about Artur Shehu.
"He is from the village of Kanina, far from here and up in the mountains," says Konomi, motioning inland, "but his family has never lived here. He's involved in shady dealings."
Then Kota speaks up. "There wasn't a single soul of that family living here, going back to the Ottoman times," she says. "But we've heard stories about him, and we're very scared of him."

Twenty years ago, Kota, Konomi and dozens of others in this village learned that Artur Shehu had somehow acquired their farmland. They filed suit in Albanian court to reclaim their land, a fight that escalated this past April when Shehu sold the 300-acre parcel that includes what they say is their farmland to a company developing a luxury resort project for Kushner.
That transaction, however, is under review.
In court documents obtained by NPR, Albanian prosecutors argue that the land involved in Kushner's development is "suspected of having been illegally acquired through forgery."

A spokesman for Kushner did not respond to NPR's request for comment by the time this article was published. Kushner had previously issued a statement on his website saying his partnership purchased the land from a private party in a private transaction. "Title was reviewed by counsel and verified," the statement says.
Shehu did not respond to NPR's request for comment. He has previously denied any wrongdoing. However, in Tirana, a former lawyer for Shehu was willing to talk.
Oceanfront properties are now claimed by several parties

"The people that Artur [Shehu] has authorized by power of attorney to deal with his family's properties committed a forgery in which they removed the property from the brother of Artur's grandfather and passed it to Artur's grandfather," says Kujtim Cakrani. "That is the whole story of the property."

Cakrani says Shehu's associates forged an inheritance certificate that made it appear that Shehu's grandfather had owned the land, which was then passed to Artur Shehu himself. And then last April, Shehu sold that land to Moutaz and Ramez Al-Khayyat, Syrian-born Qatari billionaire brothers who are financial partners of Jared Kushner.

Cakrani says that when he discovered that Artur Shehu was involved in this alleged forgery, he dropped him as his client. "I could no longer continue representing him because of the seriousness of the matter," he says. "It is impossible for me, with these documents that he has, to defend him."

And this is why, Cakrani says, Albanian state prosecutors have put Shehu under investigation and froze his bank accounts. Cakrani says he is now representing a group of 30 relatives of Shehu who he claims to be the rightful owners of this land.

Gentian Mocka, as well as Minella Konomi and Natasha Kota in Zvernec, tell NPR that nobody by the name of Shehu — neither Artur nor his relatives — has any legal claim to what they say is their land, oceanfront property that has now been claimed by several parties, including the son-in-law of the president of the United States.
Wealthy speculators have exploited land in Albania since the fall of communism
Albanian real estate law expert Roden Hoxha says he has seen this kind of land battle many times before. "But now that Kushner is in it," he says, "everybody is freaking out."

He says land ownership in Albania is complicated by decades under a Stalinist regime that stole all the land from private owners and collectivized it. When communism fell in 1991, he says Albania became a land grab free-for-all.
"It was basically chaos," he says. "People started claiming land wherever they threw a stone. It was basically the Albanian version of the U.S.' claiming of the West."

Hoxha describes wealthy speculators keen to exploit the chaos of the moment: locals whose families have farmed the land for generations and well-connected operators like Shehu, who aggressively try to claim that land. "And then on the international level," says Hoxha, most recently, "it exploded because it was Kushner and Trump and Arab money behind it."

And so, Hoxha says, what at first appeared to be yet another Albanian land dispute now has ties all the way to the White House. In the end, an Albanian court will likely decide who the rightful owner of this property is. But for now, it has sparked unprecedented public outrage in Albania. Protesters have taken to the streets of the capital, Tirana, every day since May 31, calling on Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. But Rama has only vowed to crack down harder on what have become increasingly violent demonstrations against his entire government.
Rama has also vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned, but an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.

When contacted by NPR, Elona Sinaj, Rama's spokesperson, sent a statement saying, "If the seller does not have legitimate ownership of the property, the money will remain within the Republic of Albania, and certainly it will be used for anyone who proves that his claim over the property is grounded."
Sinaj went on to say that the ambition for Rama's government is "to create a new benchmark for sustainable Mediterranean development."
Some Albanians see advantages to having a Kushner-linked resort

That goal aligns with Kushner's vision for a luxury resort — a five-star ecotourism site, as his wife, Ivanka Trump, laid out in a podcast episode called "Ivanka Trump on Building the Authentic Life."

"For me," said Trump, "this is, it feels more like a challenge than anything else, the culmination of all of my experience in real estate, all of my travel, a lot of reflection on how I want to live."
In the podcast, Trump described both the Zvernec beachfront property as well as Sazan — an uninhabited island across from it — as part of a development project belonging to her and Kushner.

Local tour operator Sherif Durmishaj has made a living taking tourists to Sazan by boat, guiding hikes past foxholes and signs along the trail that warn of active land mines scattered throughout the island's forests. For years, this island was a fortified military outpost.
Durmishaj says he's seen the ongoing protests against the Kushner project, but he takes a different view of it.

"I work in tourism, and I'm from here," he says, "and if you've seen how local developers, along with the mafia, have built this region, it's just a massacre. They've destroyed so much of what is a beautiful coastline, and I support the Kushner project because it's going to be ecologically sustainable and it will set a good benchmark for future projects."
"We are a small country," Durmishaj says, "and Kushner and Trump are very big names."
At least one big name will be in the crosshairs of the incoming Democratic Congress in the U.S.

Regarding Kushner, "This is an individual in the Trump family who has essentially been two-timing on the American people," says Maryland Democratic Rep. Jamie Raskin, who is expected to chair the House Judiciary Committee and will have the power to investigate and subpoena members of President Trump's family.
He says he'll be focusing on Kushner, who he says has been splitting his time between foreign policy and making business deals on the side.

"American foreign policy has never seen anything like that before," says Raskin. "And in this, of course, he is only imitating his father-in-law, who declared that he got $2.2 billion on the side in his first year in office. Uh, that's more than $1 million an hour."

Raskin says the luxury resort project in Albania is one of many Kushner-backed deals that have prompted investigative inquiries from his committee, and there could be more as the new U.S. Congress is sworn in in January.
Fjori Sinoruka contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Two arrested over suspected burglary at royal family’s Sandringham estate
keyFacts: British police arrested two men on suspicion of burglary following a reported break-in at the royal Sandringham estate.
The break-in occurred at Anmer Hall, a residence used by Prince William and Princess Kate, who were not present.
Princess Kate is set to feature in a television documentary about her cancer diagnosis airing on November 30.
body: LONDON — Two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the royal family’s Sandringham estate, British police said Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the country home of Prince William and Princess Kate.

Police responded to reports of “suspicious activity” at the address Monday evening, dispatching searches by police dogs, drones a helicopter. That resulted in two men being arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing, according to a statement from the Norfolk Constabulary, the local police authority. The property was unoccupied at the time of the incident, it added.

The Sun newspaper first reported that police were investigating a break-in at Anmer Hall, one of the residences used by the heir to the British throne and his wife, nestled in the heart of the royals’ sprawling estate.

Kensington Palace, which handles communications for William and Kate, said it would not comment publicly on security matters. A royal source told NBC News that the couple and their three children, George, Charlotte and Louis, were not there at the time.
The Waleses’ main home is Forest Lodge in Windsor, where they moved for a “fresh start” in 2025 after the death of Queen Elizabeth II and Kate’s cancer diagnosis.

Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country house built in the early 1800s, entered the royals’ extensive property portfolio when it was bought in 1898 by Queen Victoria’s son, who would later become King Edward VII.
It has been used by various royals over the years. And William and Kate often enjoy the residence for weekend breaks and holidays.
The incident will sharpen an ongoing debate about royal security.
William, as a “working royal,” receives 24-hour armed security. But his brother, Prince Harry, does not, having moved to California in 2020 and relinquished his regal duties.

Harry is in a protracted battle with authorities in a bid to reinstate this arrangement, which he argues is necessary due to his high-profile position and history of serving in the armed forces in Afghanistan.
This summer, Harry and his wife, Meghan, and their two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, moved back to Britain.

In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. King Charles and Queen Camilla weren’t at Windsor Castle at the time.

Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Elizabeth.

In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen’s private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

Hours after the break-in, William was meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday on the doorstep of No. 10 Downing St., where they are expected to discuss issues such as homelessness.
Meanwhile Kate is set to feature in a 30-minute documentary, “Heal,” about her cancer diagnosis and remission. It will air on NBC on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT before streaming on Peacock from Dec. 1.

articles.headline: Trump Signs Directive To Bolster, Expedite Death Penalty
keyFacts: President Donald Trump signed a memorandum directing the Justice Department to fast-track and bolster the federal death penalty.
Trump announced his administration will work to undo California Governor Gavin Newsom's commutations of 548 death row sentences.
Governor Gavin Newsom defended the commutations, criticizing Trump's pardons and highlighting racial disparities in capital punishment.
body: President Donald Trump signed a presidential memorandum on Monday aimed at fast-tracking capital punishment.

The order also tasks the Justice Department to pursue the death penalty for people convicted of first-degree murder of a minor; murder “committed in the course of rape, sexual abuse, sexual exploitation of a child, or sex trafficking”; or murder “committed in the course of kidnapping or human trafficking.”

“Once juries have spoken, capital punishment will be swift and certain,” Trump said at the Justice Department Monday. At the press conference, he also brought up Congressman Brandon Gill’s new bill, the “Just Punishment for Murder Act,” which is also aimed at bolstering the death penalty.
Despite Trump’s remarks and directive, studies show that the use of the death penalty, which is disproportionately utilized against Black men, does not deter violent crime.

Additionally, a rushed death penalty process also raises concerns about wrongly convicted people on death row. At least 200 people have been exonerated from death row since 1973, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.

Trump’s ramped-up death penalty agenda follows California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s widespread death sentence commutations, which the president condemned relentlessly on Monday. The sentences of all 548 people on California’s death row have been changed to life without the possibility of parole.
Trump said Monday his administration will work to undo Newsom’s commutations, which he called “one of the most shocking acts of injustice our country has ever seen.”
Newsom’s press office responded to the White House in a social media statement: “Every person @CAGovernor Gavin Newsom commuted from California’s death row will die in prison. Not one walks out.”

“But Donald Trump’s criminals? They walk free as wealthy donors and lobbyists secure pardons amid serious pay-to-play allegations,” the post continued. “Convicted murderers, deadly drug traffickers, violent January 6 child-sex offenders. Pardoned, released, and walking free!”
In video remarks, Newsom added: “If you’re poor, Black or brown, you get the needle. If you are rich and know Donald Trump, you get a pardon and a personal phone call.”
“A Justice Department that prosecutes his enemies and pardons himself and his friends, that’s not law enforcement, that’s a protection racket,” Newsom said, calling for pardon reform.
California had the nation’s largest death row population, but it has not executed anyone since 2006.

Trump reinstated the federal death penalty at the end of his last term, killing a record-breaking 13 people in the last six months of his first term, ending a 17-year moratorium. Biden reinstated the moratorium on the federal death penalty, but Trump signed an executive order to restore the death penalty on his first day back in office during his second term.

Public support for the death penalty has sunk to a level not seen since 1971, according to a poll by Gallup published earlier this month. The poll found that 49% of Americans supported the death penalty compared to 45% who opposed it. Republican support sat at around 73%, while Democrat support was at 28%.
The White House declined HuffPost’s request for additional comment.
